title: The model provider fails
purpose: Make the primary model provider unavailable. A run with a fallback must carry on through the fallback. A run without one must retry with backoff and recover on its own. And an operator must be able to pause every run, wait out an incident with no model call made, and resume them at a limited rate.

agentctl model-fault --seconds 0   # the provider is back
agentctl ops resume-all --rate 1   # resume them one per second

checks.description: with the primary down, the run reached the review step through the fallback
checks.because: The gateway sends the call to the fallback model when the primary does not answer. The run never saw an error.
Every row the gateway recorded for the run is a success.

checks.description: the first step was refused several times before it succeeded
checks.because: A refused call is a failed activity. The engine runs it again after 2, 4, 8 seconds and so on, until the provider answers.

checks.description: the retries were spaced out, not a burst
checks.because: The run needed 38 seconds to get past step 0, which is how long the provider was down.

checks.description: the history shows the model call taking more than one attempt
checks.because: The attempt count and the last failure are kept in the history, so an operator can see why a step was slow.
One call to the session API signals every running workflow.

checks.description: each run finished the step it was on and then stopped
checks.because: A pause is checked between steps, so no step is left half done.

checks.description: while paused, the provider received no call from any of them
checks.because: A paused run is waiting on a signal, so nothing calls the gateway: the incident is not made worse by the retries.

checks.description: the runs were resumed one per second, not all at once
checks.because: Five runs at one per second took 5.2 seconds to release.

checks.description: every run then carried on to the review step
checks.because: They continued from the step they had paused at.
